A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ImpRIF study and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-I. Content can be matched across relocation and renumbering, including the 32B ablations moved into the main text.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C report original model-training experiments, benchmark comparisons, and ablations, including Qwen3 and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B results.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds mathematics evaluations, training-difficulty experiments, and human validation of the thinking-process reward scores.

M1.justification: The ERG construction, graph-guided SFT, reward components, and GRPO procedure remain unchanged, including their equations and appendix prompts. Naming GPT-5 as the reward judge supplies implementation information without establishing a change to the method.

E1.justification: V2 extends evaluation into mathematical problem solving through MATH-Perturb, including Simple and Hard subsets, and AIME-2025 I and II (Appendix Table 10). This adds a distinct evaluation domain beyond the retained instruction-following benchmarks and LogicBench; training-data coverage remains unchanged.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in the retained experiments are unchanged. The new mathematics evaluation compares the already-used Qwen3-32B and ImpRIF-32B models; it does not introduce another baseline method.

E3.justification: V2 adds an SFT comparison using overlapping training subsets: Easy levels 1-3, Middle levels 2-4, and Hard levels 3-5 (Section 4.4). Appendix C.3 also introduces a validation procedure with 100 randomly sampled instances and three human annotators. Existing splits, training budgets, and evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: A new ablation tests how training-data difficulty affects ImpRIF-4B-SFT performance (Table 4). A separate human check assesses whether the thinking-process reward scores are reasonable (Appendix C.3). Existing complexity breakdowns, case studies, and 32B ablations are retained; moving the latter into Tables 2 and 3 adds no analysis.

E5.justification: V2 adds no repeated-run counts, random-seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures. The new 90% human-model agreement figure is a validation outcome, without accompanying uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results are unchanged. New Table 4 reports Easy/Middle/Hard CSR/ISR scores of 60.09/29.94, 62.77/31.08, and 64.77/33.41. New Table 10 reports Qwen3-32B versus ImpRIF-32B scores of 79.21 versus 81.00 on MATH-Perturb All and 70.00 versus 73.33 on AIME overall; AIME-II is tied at 73.33. Appendix C.3 adds 90% human-model agreement.

T1.justification: The graph formalization, SFT loss, reward definitions, evaluation formulas, and GRPO equations remain unchanged, including Appendix E. The added discussion of complexity indicators introduces no new formal result or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same central claims about implicit reasoning, ERG-based training, and improved complex instruction following. The new experiments supplement their evidence without redefining these core contributions.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the mathematics results as evidence of improved underlying reasoning and broader transfer (Section 4.3 and Appendix C.4). It also argues that harder training examples improve performance and discusses constraint count versus node count as complexity indicators (Section 4.4). The stated limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C.1 newly identifies GPT-5 as the judge used for thinking-process and partial rewards. Existing hyperparameters, frameworks, and prompts remain unchanged. V2 also removes the abstract's promise of future open-sourcing, without documenting an actual change in resource access.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for MATH-Perturb and AIME-2025 to support the new evaluations. The related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain substantively unchanged; MedMT and DeepSeek-R1 bibliographic updates do not introduce different underlying works.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized wording and typography corrections, expands author affiliations and contact information, adds acknowledgments, and reorganizes Appendix C around the added experiments. The overall narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: V1 Appendix Tables 9 and 10 are merged into v2 main Tables 2 and 3. V2 adds the training-difficulty and mathematics tables, relocates existing figures and dataset tables, and adjusts page flow. The figures retain their substantive designs and content.

improvement.justification: V2 provides useful additional support through mathematics-transfer evaluations, a training-difficulty ablation, and a 100-instance human check of reward scores. Naming GPT-5 also improves implementation transparency. These are bounded gains around an unchanged method and unchanged original results: the new analyses provide limited procedural detail and no uncertainty estimates, so they modestly strengthen the paper rather than resolve its broader evidential limitations.
